profile.seconds: 20 for ascending candidate sweep; 60 for matched baseline/candidate pair

notes: Baseline production binary predates runtime payload retention; candidate connects bounded repair and retains submitted payloads until acknowledged or expired.
Candidate ascending sweep: nine twenty-second points, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, 21 Gbit/s requested each direction, then unlimited.
Matched sequences: three sixty-second points, 21 Gbit/s, unlimited, 21 Gbit/s return, for baseline then candidate.
No builds, tests or repository packing overlapped throughput measurements.
Goodput excludes drain; missing fractions and counter deltas include drain. CPU 100% is one core.
Repair can reorder complete frames. Nonzero admission pressure, duplicate pieces and reordering are recorded rather than rejected by the parser.
A locally retried packed datagram can count already retained pieces as duplicate pieces; this counter is not a network-repair volume estimate.
Expiry may follow successful peer TAP delivery if ACK feedback is lost. Counter units differ and cannot be summed into missing-frame counts.

The first candidate ascending attempt exited with ConnectionRefused before a complete dataset. Failure logs were not retained; its cause is unconfirmed and it is excluded. The reported retry completed all nine points.
The later source-deadline fix is not present in any observation in this file.
